newsitem.title: USA: Stone sees demand and prices improving.
newsitem.headline: Stone sees demand and prices improving.

text.p: Stone Container Corp, reporting a loss for the 1996 fourth quarter and full year, said Monday it sees industry indicators pointing toward renewed growth and profitability in 1997.

"Demand for our unbleached paper and packaging products began to improve in the second half of (1996), absorbing much of the additional industry capacity, returning inventories to manageable levels and stabilizing prices," said Roger Stone, chairman, president and chief executive officer, in a statement.

"At the same time, demand growth is expected to exceed capacity growth in 1997 and beyond, and containerboard exports, which were very strong in 1996, are expected to continue to grow in 1997," he said.
"We are now seeing prices stabilize for publication papers, as demand is improving and inventories are returning to more normal levels," he said.

He said the company announced a price increase for newsprint to take effect during February, and an increase in export linerboard prices effective March 1. Company officials were not available to provide details on the increases.
"We expect that, with moderate economic growth and continued strong demand, we will see a return to more normal pricing across our product lines as 1997 progresses," he said.

Stone reported a 1996 fourth quarter loss of $86.4 million or $0.89 a share compared with profits of $79.7 million or $0.73 in the year earlier quarter. For all of 1996, Stone reported a loss of $126.2 million or $1.35 compared with a profit of $255.5 million or $2.24.
Sharply lower selling prices for Stone's core products and significant market-related downtime at its pulp and paper mills hurt 1996 fourth quarter and full year results, it said.

In response to market conditions, Stone said it removed more than 435,000 short tons of containerboard and more than 250,000 short tons of market pulp from production in 1996. In addition, Stone-Consolidated Corp, Stone's publication papers affiliate, removed more than 208,000 metric tons of publication papers from production due to market conditions in 1996.
Stone said its liquidity and cash position are at high levels. During the year, the company said it extended some of its debt maturities and in many cases reduced its net interest costs.
"Debt reduciton and a nomalization of ourbalance sheet reamin very high prioroties for the company," said Raldolph Read, chief financial and planning officer, in a statement.
Stone produces paper, paper packaging, containerbaord, corrugated contaienrs, kraft paper, paper bags and through its investment in Stone-Consolidated Corp, publication papers.
Shares of Stone were trading unchanged at 13-1/8.
